title: Florida House, District 61
what_it_does: Represents District 61 (Parts of Hillsborough, Pinellas) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings.

candidates.name: Linda Chaney
candidates.background: Qualified for the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot according to the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list (Qualified).

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F in the June 2026 special session, which placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot to raise the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and to limit how counties and cities may spend property-tax revenue.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30

abortion.summary: Voted yes on SB 300 (2023), the law that limits most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit), passage 70-40

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which removed income limits and enrollment caps so state scholarship funds can follow any K-12 student to private or home education.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (universal school-choice scholarships), passage 83-27

growth.summary: Chaney did not return the Times questionnaire. The paper reported she voted for Senate Bill 484, which requires public disclosure of new data-center projects and lets local governments set stricter land-use rules for them.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

taxes.summary: The Times quoted Chaney's campaign site saying the local economy should be revived by lowering taxes and cutting regulations, and that infrastructure can be rebuilt without raising taxes.
taxes.quote: I know we can rebuild our infrastructure without raising taxes.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

environment.summary: Chaney's campaign site, quoted by the Times, lists the environment among her three top priorities: preserving the beaches and protecting water quality, while saying this can be done without interfering in the economics of tourism.
environment.quote: We must preserve and protect our pristine beaches, protect our water quality...

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

energy.summary: Voted for CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

lgbtq.summary: Voted for SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.

SB 254 (2023) roll-call vote (House)

elections.summary: Voted for SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

SB 7050 (2023) roll-call vote (House)

candidates.name: May Thach
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Civic-engagement organizer; former Peace Corps volunteer
candidates.background: St. Petersburg resident whose family immigrated to the U.S. in 1999; she was raised by a single mother with four siblings. A University of South Florida graduate with a graduate degree from UC San Diego, she served four years as a Peace Corps volunteer in Zambia and later built a statewide civic-engagement coalition in Asian American and Pacific Islander communities.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

insurance.summary: Thach said she would cap insurance rate hikes, tax insurers' excess profits and return them to policyholders, and expand state-backed universal windstorm coverage.
insurance.quote: Capping insurance rate hikes. Taxing insurance companies on their excess profits and returning them to policyholders. Expanding our state-backed universal windstorm coverage.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

housing.summary: She calls for stronger tenant protections as part of lowering costs.

sources.title: May Thach for Florida House (campaign website)

healthcare.summary: She supports expanding Medicaid and keeping politicians out of private health-care decisions.
healthcare.quote: expanding Medicaid, keeping politicians out of private healthcare decisions

sources.title: May Thach for Florida House (campaign website)

abortion.summary: She says politicians should be kept out of private health-care decisions; she does not name the six-week law.

sources.title: May Thach for Florida House (campaign website)

education_choice.summary: She calls for increasing accountability in school voucher programs.
education_choice.quote: increasing accountability in school voucher programs

sources.title: May Thach for Florida House (campaign website)

elections.summary: She supports expanding voter access and government transparency.
elections.quote: expanding voter access, increasing government transparency

sources.title: May Thach for Florida House (campaign website)

environment.summary: She wants practical solutions to help communities prepare for severe weather and reduce flooding.

sources.title: May Thach for Florida House (campaign website)

growth.summary: Thach told the Times Florida should have a moratorium on the development of any new hyperscale data centers, with regulations on noise, water and electricity use and a role for communities in the approval process.
growth.quote: Florida should have a moratorium on the development of any new hyperscale data centers.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

taxes.summary: Thach said she would raise the minimum wage to $20 an hour and pursue tax reforms closing corporate loopholes so corporations 'pay their fair share,' rather than broad tax cuts.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)
